description: The Věstník ČNB hub URL advertised in the legislativní základna link list, https://www.cnb.cz/cs/o_cnb/legislativa_vestnik-cnb/, returned HTTP 404 on fetch. Working access appears to be via per-year pages under /cs/legislativa/vestnik-cnb/vestnik-cnb-rocnik-YYYY/ and direct PDF paths under /export/sites/cnb/cs/legislativa/.galleries/Vestnik-CNB/YYYY/.

result.result_summary: 404 on the hub path; per-year and per-částka URLs recovered from search results instead. Recorded as moved, NOT dead — the Věstník is plainly still being issued (částka 4/2026 dated 18 June 2026 was surfaced).

why_it_matters: The Věstník is the legally authentic publication channel for úřední sdělení and opatření. A collector built on the stale hub URL would silently miss the entire authentic corpus, so the per-year URL pattern must be the entry point and needs deterministic verification.

description: No open-data API, bulk download, or structured (JSON/XML) endpoint for the ČNB regulatory corpus was found in this pass. Searches surfaced only HTML pages, PDF documents and an RSS index; ČNB's own RSS note explicitly excludes the application-driven sections (Seznamy a evidence, Pravomocná rozhodnutí, Informace zveřejňované emitenty).

result.result_summary: Collection for this cell must be assumed to be HTML/PDF scraping plus RSS, not API ingestion, until a dedicated open-data pass proves otherwise.

why_it_matters: Sets the engineering cost and fragility profile for the whole ČNB cell, and means the three RSS-excluded registers each need bespoke collectors.

description: No single ČNB page was found that consolidates regulatory application dates / compliance deadlines for banks and payment institutions. Deadline information is scattered across the consultation register (comment-period end dates), individual vyhlášky (účinnost), SDAT methodology change notes, the ESA-guidelines comply-or-explain notices (application dates), and the event calendar.

result.result_summary: A deadline view must be synthesised by the pipeline from at least five separate ČNB sources; it cannot be lifted from one page.

why_it_matters: Deadlines are an explicit topic of this run. Assuming a single authoritative deadline page exists would produce a systematically incomplete calendar.

description: 'Opatření obecné povahy' is a generic Czech administrative-law instrument used by many public bodies. Searching it without a ČNB qualifier returns Český telekomunikační úřad, Ministerstvo vnitra land-use measures, and Supreme Administrative Court case law. Similarly 'vyhláška' alone is near-useless. 'Dohledový benchmark', by contrast, is a high-precision ČNB-specific term.

result.result_summary: Query design for this cell must pin the actor (ČNB / Česká národní banka) or the sector, or rely on the ČNB-unique terms.

why_it_matters: Prevents wasted collection cycles and false-positive sources in any automated query expansion built on these seed terms.

description: The ČNB consultation register (/cs/legislativa/konzultacni-materialy-a-navrhy/) is dominated in volume by draft vyhlášky for commemorative coins and banknotes rather than by financial-regulation drafts; the most recent entry observed (10 February 2026) was a commemorative gold coin.

result.result_summary: Roughly the majority of recent entries are numismatic. Financial-regulation drafts (bank reporting, PSP incident and fraud reporting, supervision amendments effective January 2026) are present but interleaved.

why_it_matters: An unfiltered alerting rule on this page will be mostly false positives and will be ignored by analysts; keyword filtering is mandatory at ingestion.

description: ČNB maintains a parallel /en/ site with the same sectoral structure, but the English corpus is a selective subset: only some RS opinions have -EN pages, dohledové benchmarky were found only as Czech PDFs, and the Věstník částky are Czech-only. ČNB itself states the authentic wording is the Czech Sbírka zákonů / Věstník version.

result.result_summary: English-only collection would miss the authentic legal texts and most supervisory-expectation material. Czech-language collection is structurally mandatory for this cell.

why_it_matters: Directly validates the run's mandatory-local-language rule and dictates that OCR/NLP for this cell must handle Czech, including diacritics-stripped variants in URLs and filenames.

description: ČNB does not appear to operate a separate 'open public consultations with countdown' register in the style of EBA/ESMA. Consultation-type material is interleaved with draft decrees (including a large volume of commemorative-coin vyhlášky) on the single Konzultační materiály a návrhy page.

result.result_summary: The index observed is dominated by numismatic decree drafts; substantive prudential/payments drafts are a minority of entries and comment deadlines are expressed inline as free text rather than as a structured field.

why_it_matters: Any collector must filter aggressively by subject and parse deadlines from prose; a naive feed will be mostly coin decrees and will miss the structured comment window entirely.

description: English-language searching for ČNB consultations returned mostly EBA/ESMA material rather than ČNB's own; the ČNB EN site carries a supervision news section but no evident English mirror of the konzultační materiály index.

result.result_summary: English queries surfaced cnb.cz/en/supervision-financial-market/news/ and .../supervisory-official-information-and-benchmarks/ but no EN consultation index.

why_it_matters: Confirms that Czech-language monitoring is mandatory for this cell; an English-only pipeline would miss essentially all CZ comment windows.

description: No consolidated, machine-readable ČNB 'supervisory reporting deadline calendar' (ICS/API/JSON) was found for regulated entities. Deadlines are dispersed across the vyhlášky, per-collection SDAT descriptions, and the Harmonogram XLS (which covers ČNB's own publications, not obligors' due dates).

result.result_summary: Searches on kalendář sběrů / harmonogram výkaznictví returned narrative pages and an XLS of ČNB publication dates, not an obligor deadline feed.

why_it_matters: The reporting-timetable half of this cell must be reconstructed by the collector from decree text plus SDAT collection descriptions — it cannot simply be ingested.

description: Several candidate URLs were reached only via search-result metadata or a summarising fetch, not confirmed page-by-page in this pass; one mirrored host (cnb.sp.cz.net) appeared in results and looks like a proxy/mirror rather than the canonical cnb.cz origin and should not be collected from.

result.result_summary: Only https://www.cnb.cz/cs/legislativa/konzultacni-materialy-a-navrhy/ was directly fetched and read in this pass; the rest rest on search-engine evidence.

why_it_matters: Liveness and canonicality must be settled by the deterministic verification pass; a 403/timeout on cnb.cz should be read as bot defence, not as a dead source.

description: No CZ bank or PSP was found publishing a machine-readable, standardised changelog feed (RSS/JSON) for regulatory-driven T&C or API changes. Air Bank's dated HTML list is the closest to a true changelog; most institutions publish change notices as loose dated PDFs or one-off news items.

result.result_summary: Searches in cs and en for bank API release-notes/changelog feeds returned portal landing pages and third-party trackers, not feeds.

why_it_matters: Collection for this cell must be built on HTML/PDF diffing and filename-date parsing, not feed subscription; effort estimates should assume per-institution custom extractors.

description: Several CZ bank developer portals (MONETA apiportal.moneta.cz, Raiffeisenbank production APIs, Erste sandbox) appear to place specifications and change notices behind TPP registration or licence checks, so change calendars may not be publicly observable.

result.result_summary: Search results and portal descriptions repeatedly reference registration/licence prerequisites; MONETA documentation described as not yet published.

why_it_matters: Bottom-up dating of PSD2 technical deadlines will be systematically incomplete for gated banks; corroboration must lean on integrator commentary and the banks' public client notices.

description: https://www.apiportal.cz/ — the aggregator recommended by the cz-banking-psd2 repo — refused connection during this run.

result.result_summary: connect ECONNREFUSED on TLS port 443; no HTTP status obtained.

why_it_matters: This is a hypothesis, not a verdict: the site may be bot-defended or the failure transient. It should be re-tested by the deterministic liveness pass before being deprioritised.

description: No single settled Czech term exists for 'API change calendar' or 'deprecation notice'. Observed variants include 'aktuálně k API', 'ukončení podpory', 'končí zastaralé endpointy', 'přechod na nové verze', 'změny v API'. English-in-Czech ('release notes', 'changelog', 'sandbox', 'developer portál', 'endpoint') is common but inconsistent.

result.result_summary: cs queries needed multiple phrasings to surface the same class of document; no canonical keyword.

why_it_matters: Keyword-based monitoring must use a disjunctive multilingual pattern set, or it will miss deprecation notices at banks using non-standard wording.

description: For the instant-payments regulation (EU) 2024/886, I found the regulation itself and general reporting, plus an indication that UniCredit announced VOP/sazebník changes in connection with instant payments, but did not reach a bank-published notice page that explicitly cites 2024/886 as the reason for a fee-schedule change.

result.result_summary: cs query on sazebník changes citing 2024/886 returned regulator/EUR-Lex/press sources rather than a bank notice document.

why_it_matters: The cell's core hypothesis — that bank notices cite the exact legal instrument — is plausible and partially evidenced (Air Bank citing SEPA rules) but not yet confirmed for the 2024/886 case; targeted PDF full-text search across bank notice archives is needed.

description: Searches combining Lupa.cz / Seznam Zprávy / iROZHLAS with 'ČNB pokuta bance', 'dohled', 'fintech zpřísnění' returned only cnb.cz pages, not articles from those outlets.

result.result_summary: General web search does not surface these outlets' regulatory articles well; their content appears under-indexed for these query shapes.

why_it_matters: Collection for these three must go through their own on-site search / RSS rather than general web search, or coverage of them will look thinner than it is.

description: Section URLs for Seznam Zprávy economics (seznamzpravy.cz/sekce/ekonomika-16) and iROZHLAS economics (irozhlas.cz/ekonomika) were inferred from site conventions, not observed in results, and were not fetched in this pass.

result.result_summary: Homepage domains are well attested; deep section paths are hypotheses.

why_it_matters: The deterministic liveness pass should resolve the correct section/RSS paths before these are wired into collection.

description: Hospodářské noviny (hn.cz) and the print edition of Bankovnictví are subscription-gated; Bankovnictví sells predplatne, HN uses a hard paywall.

result.result_summary: Highest-value Czech regulatory journalism is largely behind paywalls.

why_it_matters: A licensed subscription or a Czech media-monitoring service (Anopress/Newton) is likely required for full-text A3 coverage; headline-only monitoring will miss the substance.

description: Investujeme.cz did not appear in any result set for the fintech/payment-regulation queries run.

result.result_summary: Could not confirm current activity or regulatory coverage of that outlet in this pass.

why_it_matters: Should be checked directly rather than assumed live or assumed dead.

description: English-language queries about Czech banking-rule changes were not productive relative to Czech ones; the cell rationale that English CZ coverage is thin and lagging is consistent with what was observed.

result.result_summary: Czech-language querying carried essentially all the discovery value in this cell.

why_it_matters: Any downstream collection design that relies on English feeds will systematically miss Czech regulatory signals.

description: No official, legally binding English-language consolidated corpus of Czech law was found. e-Sbírka publishes Czech only; English texts of banking/payments acts exist only as informative regulator translations of uncertain vintage.

result.result_summary: English-language searching surfaced regulator translations and commentary, not a state-guaranteed EN corpus.

why_it_matters: Any EN-driven pipeline will silently lag the binding CZ text; effective dates and deadlines must always be resolved against the Czech version.

description: The e-Sbírka public API and open data were announced as live from 15 January 2024, but multiple sources report the open data is published without proper documentation.

result.result_summary: Announcement page and MV FOI responses confirm the API exists; no complete schema documentation located in this pass.

why_it_matters: Machine ingestion of the authoritative corpus will require reverse-engineering endpoints and response shapes, and is exposed to unannounced breaking changes.

description: eKLEP (apps.odok.cz/eklep) — the internal legislative library — is explicitly not intended for the public; only VeKLEP content is exposed.

result.result_summary: Documented as non-public; no public credential path found.

why_it_matters: Some pre-consultation drafts and internal comment resolutions are invisible until they surface in VeKLEP, capping how early the pipeline can be seen.

description: Webarchiv NK ČR's full holdings are accessible only from terminals inside the National Library; only contractually cleared selective-harvest sites are served online.

result.result_summary: Confirmed in Webarchiv's own 'O Webarchivu' and FAQ pages.

why_it_matters: The national archive cannot be the automated fallback for rotted regulator URLs; Internet Archive must carry that role, with a known coverage risk for CZ-only pages.

description: e-Sbírka has been publicly reported (Jan 2024) to be missing some recent regulations at launch, and commentary questions its completeness.

result.result_summary: Press reporting flags missing recent predpisy; not independently verified here.

why_it_matters: Completeness of the authoritative corpus cannot be assumed; a second corpus (Zákony pro lidi / Esipa) is needed as a reconciliation check.

description: Věstník ČNB is published in full online only from volume 2001 onward; earlier volumes exist in printed form in the ČNB specialist library.

result.result_summary: Stated on the ČNB Věstník page.

why_it_matters: Deadline and supervisory-notice series cannot be reconstructed digitally before 2001 without a manual library visit.

description: No dedicated data.gov.cz dataset specifically for ČNB regulatory acts/Věstník was located in this pass; ČNB regulatory publication appears not to be catalogued as open data.

result.result_summary: Catalogue-level searching surfaced e-Sbírka open data and general legal-framework articles only.

why_it_matters: Věstník ČNB and ČNB decree pages must be scraped from HTML/PDF; there is no structured feed for the central bank's own instruments.

description: No standalone, separately published ČNB 'thematic review' report series (analogous to ECB/EBA thematic reviews) was located during this pass. Thematic assessment appears to be described inside the supervisory strategy page and reported within the annual Zpráva o výkonu dohledu and the Dohledová úřední sdělení a benchmarky series, rather than as its own publication series with its own index page.

result.result_summary: Searches on 'tematické šetření' / 'tematická kontrola' returned the supervisory strategy page and benchmark series, not a dedicated thematic-review index.

why_it_matters: Collection design should not assume a dedicated thematic-review feed exists for CZ; thematic findings must be extracted from the annual supervisory report and the numbered supervisory communications instead.

description: A dedicated ČNB 'úřední deska' (official notice board) page collecting all opatření obecné povahy in one dated feed was not identified. The Czech query for it returned other public bodies' notice boards (SÚJB, Ministry of Interior, municipalities) and the CCyB-specific provision index on cnb.cz.

result.result_summary: The CCyB provisions are indexed under the macroprudential policy tree; no cross-cutting ČNB notice-board index surfaced.

why_it_matters: If no single notice-board feed exists, monitoring must be per-instrument (CCyB, systemic risk buffer, O-SII, credit indicators) rather than one consolidated legal-acts feed, which raises the risk of missing an instrument added later.

description: The ESRB national-measures database / EBA CCyB rate register entry for the Czech Republic was not directly located in this pass; the search for it returned only ČNB's own pages. The ESRB is referenced by ČNB as an input to its buffer-guide methodology, so an ESRB-side register very likely exists, but I did not reach it and will not assert its URL.

result.result_summary: Query returned cnb.cz results exclusively; no esrb.europa.eu or eba.europa.eu URL confirmed.

why_it_matters: An EU-level register would give cross-country comparability and an independent confirmation channel for CZ buffer rates and effective dates; it remains an open discovery item.

description: No RSS/Atom or API endpoint for ČNB supervision or financial-stability news was confirmed. The RSS-oriented Czech query returned no ČNB feed URL.

result.result_summary: RSS subscription path for cnb.cz news/supervision remains unverified.

why_it_matters: Absent a confirmed feed, collection must rely on HTML listing polling, which is more brittle and needs change-detection logic.

description: Ministry of Finance content appears under both mfcr.cz and mf.gov.cz, with recent Zpráva o vývoji finančního trhu pages on mf.gov.cz and older ones on mfcr.cz.

result.result_summary: Both hostnames returned live-looking URLs for the same report series across different years.

why_it_matters: Stored MF URLs may silently rot; the collector should normalise/redirect-follow between the two hosts rather than treat an mfcr.cz miss as a dead source.

description: Searched for CZ payment/banking technology vendors (Trask, Comarch, Asseco, Sonet, MONET+, Profinit) running Czech-language RegTech webinars that name upcoming CZ obligations (e.g. Verification of Payee, SEPA Instant deadlines).

result.result_summary: No CZ-vendor webinar landing pages surfaced in search; results were dominated by non-CZ webinar platforms (Banking Exchange, RedCompass Labs). Vendor webinar pages appear to live behind marketing sites or LinkedIn events that general search does not index well.

why_it_matters: Vendor readiness webinars are the most deadline-explicit part of this cell's rationale; missing them weakens the 'vendors advertise deadlines to sell readiness' signal.

description: Attempted to locate structured CZ banking compliance job-ad results naming specific regulations (PSD3, DORA, MiCA, VoP) on jobs.cz and LinkedIn via search.

result.result_summary: Only aggregator landing pages and Glassdoor/Indeed roll-ups were retrievable; individual ad text naming regulations was visible mostly in secondary boards. Job boards are query-driven and largely invisible to general web search.

why_it_matters: The hiring signal must be collected by direct parameterised querying of each board rather than by search-engine discovery, which changes the collection design and the ToS exposure.

description: Looked for a canonical, permanently archived programme for 'Trendy v platebním styku' and CARDFORUM on the organisers' own domains.

result.result_summary: Trendy programme content was found only via a third-party aggregator page; CARDFORUM programmes appear as year-stamped PDFs under cardforum.cz/data/ with no visible index page. Neither was confirmed as a stable archive.

why_it_matters: Multi-year agenda trend analysis may require third-party mirrors and PDF-pattern guessing rather than a reliable archive endpoint.

description: No established Czech-language term surfaced for 'RegTech webinar' as a distinct product category; searches on 'webinář regtech' returned generic regulatory-news articles rather than a webinar channel.

result.result_summary: The Czech market appears to label these as 'odborný seminář', 'školení' or 'webinář' plus the regulation acronym (DORA, PSD3, AML), not as 'regtech'.

why_it_matters: Query design for ongoing collection must use obligation acronyms plus generic training nouns; 'regtech' is a low-yield term in Czech and would cause silent under-collection.

description: Several sources were identified only through search-result metadata and not fetched (cardforum.cz root, fintechroadmap.cz, kursy.cz, financnictvi.konference.cz, mfcr.cz events).

result.result_summary: URLs are recorded with confidence scores but liveness was not tested here; any of them could be moved or bot-defended.

why_it_matters: Downstream deterministic verification must resolve these; a failure should be treated as a hypothesis (bot defence or move), not as a dead source.

description: The seven ČNB open-data CSV datasets cover banks, exchange offices, consumer-credit providers and credit intermediaries, but NOT payment institutions, e-money institutions, small-scale payment service providers (PSMR) or small-scale e-money issuers.

result.result_summary: Searched the Otevřená data page and the payments legislation landing page in cs; found no p_seznam CSV endpoint for platební instituce. Those lists appear reachable only through the JERRS UI or WS JERRS.

why_it_matters: The payments half of the run scope has no free bulk feed; collection must go through WS JERRS (certificate-gated) or careful UI querying, which changes the effort and legal profile of the pipeline.

description: WS JERRS, the only officially sanctioned machine interface to the full register, requires an electronically signed application to jerrsws@cnb.cz and authentication with a commercial qualified certificate (eIdentity, I.CA, Postsignum or an EU trust-list CA).

result.result_summary: Confirmed from the ČNB WS JERRS documentation page. No anonymous or API-key tier was found.

why_it_matters: Onboarding lead time and a certificate purchase sit between us and the best data source in this cell; it must be started early rather than discovered at build time.

description: The final-decisions application at abok.cnb.cz was identified only from a link on the ČNB pravomocná rozhodnutí hub; its search interface, query parameters and whether it exposes structured export were not inspected in this pass.

result.result_summary: Not fetched. Treated as unverified, not dead.

why_it_matters: Enforcement decisions are the core of the sanctions half of this cell; the ingestion design cannot be finalised until the application's interface is examined.

description: No single consolidated, machine-readable list of ČNB sanctions across all sectors was found; publication duties are fragmented across at least 11 separate sectoral statutes with differing retention rules (e.g. AML decisions published for 5 years after finality, insurance licence withdrawals within 30 days).

result.result_summary: Confirmed by reading the pravomocná rozhodnutí hub, which enumerates the legal bases one by one rather than pointing to a unified register.

why_it_matters: Any enforcement time series we build must reconcile heterogeneous, time-limited publication regimes, or it will understate historical AML sanctions.

description: The Czech word 'seznam' is highly ambiguous — Seznam.cz is the dominant Czech search engine, so queries containing 'seznam' return search-engine and unrelated commercial pages.

result.result_summary: The first cs query returned a search.seznam.cz result and a logistics academy page among the top hits.

why_it_matters: Future automated query generation for this cell should pair 'seznam' with disambiguating tokens ('ČNB', 'regulovaných subjektů', 'JERRS') or scope searches to cnb.cz.

description: No Czech-language MF ČR page announcing a concrete PSD3/PSR transposition draft or consultation was located, despite the EU texts reportedly being agreed and published. English-language search returned only international law-firm commentary, and Czech search returned only older payments-act amendments (2012, 2016, 2019, 2021).

result.result_summary: PSD3/PSR CZ transposition work appears not yet publicly visible on MF channels as of this scouting pass, or it is filed under an omnibus 'změna některých zákonů v oblasti finančního trhu' title that keyword search did not surface.

why_it_matters: The cell's core early-warning promise is seeing payments statute change months ahead; if the PSD3 vehicle is invisible to keyword search, monitoring must be structural (poll all MF-authored VeKLEP materials) rather than keyword-driven.

description: No documented public API or open-data dump for VeKLEP/eKLEP legislative materials was found; open-data/API documentation located covers e-Sbírka and e-Legislativa (Ministry of Interior), not the ODok comment-procedure system.

result.result_summary: eKLEP/VeKLEP will likely need HTML scraping keyed on the PID identifier; e-Sbírka has proper APIs.

why_it_matters: Determines collection engineering cost and fragility for the single highest-value source in this cell.

description: Czech government sites are mid-migration across parallel domains: mfcr.cz vs mf.gov.cz, apps.odok.cz vs odok.gov.cz, isap.vlada.cz vs isap.gov.cz, vlada.cz vs vlada.gov.cz. Both variants currently appear in search results for the same content.

result.result_summary: Multiple live aliases per source; URL stability cannot be assumed.

why_it_matters: Naive liveness checks and stored URLs will rot; the collector should canonicalise to the .gov.cz variants and tolerate redirects rather than marking sources dead.

description: MF ČR, ODok/VeKLEP, PSP.cz, Senát and e-Sbírka publish legislative material essentially only in Czech; no equivalent English legislative pipeline feed was found. English-language searching returned only private law-firm and consultancy commentary.

result.result_summary: English-only monitoring of this cell is not viable.

why_it_matters: Confirms Czech-language NLP/keyword lists are a hard requirement for A3 coverage rather than a nice-to-have.

description: No candidate URL in this slice was fetched-and-confirmed by this agent; all were derived from search-engine result listings and their titles/snippets.

result.result_summary: All URLs are provided as hypotheses for the deterministic liveness pass, not as verified endpoints.

why_it_matters: Prevents downstream over-trust; ISAP (Lotus Domino) and senat.cz (xqw/xervlet) in particular use fragile URL schemes likely to require session handling.

description: No single official CZ or EU page was found that consolidates 'EU act -> Czech application date' for the payments/digital-finance file. ČNB publishes per-instrument pages, ISAP tracks transposition per CELEX, EUR-Lex holds the article text — but the join has to be constructed by the collector.

result.result_summary: Searches in cs and en returned per-instrument pages only; no CZ regulatory calendar/timeline artefact surfaced.

why_it_matters: The deliverable of this cell (a CZ-binding deadline timetable) cannot be scraped from one place; it must be assembled from EUR-Lex CS + ČNB sdělení + ISAP, which raises collection cost and makes date-conflict reconciliation a design requirement.

description: No Czech-language version of EBA consultation papers or EBA compliance tables was found. EBA consults and publishes compliance tables in English only; only final guidelines get CS translations, and those appear with a lag via ČNB.

result.result_summary: cs queries for 'EBA konzultace' style terms returned only ČNB sdělení pages and CS PDFs of already-final guidelines.

why_it_matters: Any monitoring confined to Czech-language sources structurally misses the 2-3 month consultation window — the only period in which the eventual CZ obligation can still be influenced or anticipated.

description: The canonical index URLs for (a) the EBA consultation-paper register and (b) the EBA guideline compliance tables were not pinned down in this pass; only the parent Single Rulebook and generic search pages were confirmed in results.

result.result_summary: Search returned Single Rulebook, ISRB and Q&A pages but not a stable consultations/compliance-tables index path.

why_it_matters: These two are high-value for the cell; a verification pass should resolve them via eba.europa.eu site navigation rather than guessing paths, to avoid recording a fabricated or stale URL.

description: PSD3/PSR has no CELEX identifier or Czech official text yet — reporting indicates provisional political agreement (late 2025) with OJ publication expected during 2026 and application roughly 18-21 months later.

result.result_summary: All PSD3/PSR timeline detail found was secondary (law firms, Worldline), not primary EU text.

why_it_matters: Every PSD3/PSR date currently in circulation is provisional. The source plan must include a trigger that switches from commentary to EUR-Lex CS the day the OJ publication appears, or the intelligence product will carry unsourced dates.

description: The Czech-language ČNB CERTIS instant-payments URL slug was not directly confirmed; only the English mirror (/en/payments/certis/instant-payments/) appeared in results.

result.result_summary: EN pages confirmed; CS equivalent inferred from ČNB's consistent cs/en mirroring but not observed.

why_it_matters: Recorded as inferred, not verified — the liveness pass should resolve the cs slug from ČNB navigation.

description: No RSS/Atom or API endpoint for FAÚ aktuality, metodické pokyny or sanctions notices was located during this pass. MZV's sanctions-list section does expose an .rss URL, but nothing equivalent was found on fau.gov.cz.

result.result_summary: FAÚ change-detection will likely require HTML/PDF diffing rather than feed subscription.

why_it_matters: Deadline tracking for obliged entities depends on catching FAÚ notices quickly; without a feed the collector needs frequent polling and robust PDF hashing.

description: No public FAÚ register of individual inspection outcomes, sanctions decisions or fines against named obliged entities was found; enforcement appears to be disclosed only in aggregate via the annual report, and MP numbering shows gaps (no MP č. 2 or č. 10 listed on the current index).

result.result_summary: Entity-level AML enforcement history for Czech banks and payment institutions is not directly obtainable from FAÚ.

why_it_matters: Enforcement-pressure analysis must rely on aggregate statistics plus indirect legal-press reporting; entity-level attribution should not be promised.

description: MoneyWeb, the primary secure STR submission channel, is accessible only after a cooperation agreement and VPN tunnel with FAÚ; MoneyWeb Lite is a distributed desktop client.

result.result_summary: Only the public documentation of the reporting channel is collectable, not the channel itself.

why_it_matters: Any claim about reporting formats/schemas must be sourced from public documentation; do not attempt access to the application.

description: The Czech central inter-ministerial comment procedure portal for draft AML legislation (ODOK / VeKLEP, eklep.vlada.cz) was referenced in the seed query but was not directly located or fetched in this pass; the AMLZ amendment drafts were only observed via MF pages and secondary legal commentary.

result.result_summary: The authoritative CZ pre-legislative consultation venue for AML bills remains unconfirmed for this cell.

why_it_matters: Consultations are an explicit run topic; missing the eKLEP/VeKLEP and Poslanecká sněmovna (psp.cz) bill-tracking layer would lose the earliest visibility on new AML obligations.

description: No Czech industry-side AML source (Česká bankovní asociace AML commission outputs, Czech Fintech Association, or a compliance-officer professional body) was confirmed with a specific working URL in this pass.

result.result_summary: The industry-response side of the FAÚ regulation stream is currently unmapped in this cell.

why_it_matters: Industry commentary on draft guidance often reveals implementation cost and timing friction that neither FAÚ nor ČNB publishes.

description: The ÚOHS 'Platební styk' page (fetched) describes the IFR supervisory mandate but links no dedicated register of payment-systems decisions, methodologies or press releases; the only 'sborníky rozhodnutí' page located sits under the public-procurement methodology branch.

result.result_summary: No confirmed URL for an ÚOHS competition/payments decision search interface was found in this pass.

why_it_matters: Without a decision register, interchange/card enforcement can only be tracked via press releases, which under-report settled or minor cases.

description: The ÚOOÚ banking-sector inspection pages surfaced were from 2005, 2006 and 2016 cycles; no recent (2023-2026) bank- or PSP-specific ÚOOÚ inspection or fine page was confirmed in this pass.

result.result_summary: Recent banking-sector GDPR enforcement items exist in aggregate statistics (annual report) but were not located as individual sectoral pages.

why_it_matters: Current enforcement intensity against banks is the actionable signal; only historical sectoral pages were confirmed.

description: ČOI appears under both coi.cz and coi.gov.cz, and Kancelář finančního arbitra under both finarbitr.cz and finarbitr.gov.cz; a test/staging mirror (coi-test.bzcompany.cz) also appears in search results.

result.result_summary: Canonical domain not conclusively determined; no liveness claim made.

why_it_matters: Collection pipelines could duplicate or point at a non-canonical/staging host if the domain is not pinned during verification.

description: No RSS/Atom, API or open-data endpoint was confirmed for ÚOOÚ, NÚKIB, ÚOHS or ČOI publication streams in this pass.

result.result_summary: Collection will likely require HTML crawling and PDF extraction rather than feeds.

why_it_matters: Affects pipeline cost and change-detection reliability for deadline tracking.

description: English-language searching surfaces mainly advisory commentary; the authoritative material (ZKB 264/2025 Sb., vyhláška 408/2025 Sb., inspection protocols, arbitrator nálezy) is Czech-only.

result.result_summary: English-only collection would miss essentially all primary content in this cell.

why_it_matters: Confirms cs-language crawling and NLP must be first-class in the pipeline for this cell.

description: Neither cbaonline.cz nor its /en mirror exposed a browsable 'Stanoviska' / 'Připomínky' / 'Position papers' section in the navigation returned by fetching the homepage, /o-nas and /bankovni-regulace. Regulatory commentary appears to be dispersed across news articles, press releases and the codes-and-standards library instead.

result.result_summary: ČBA's formal consultation responses are not published as a discrete, indexed collection on its own site — unlike ČLFA (/pro-odbornou-verejnost/stanoviska-clfa) and AKAT (/Dokumenty/Dokumenty-AKAT).

why_it_matters: A3 collection for ČBA cannot rely on a positions index; it must be assembled from ODOK vypořádání tables, EBA/EC consultation archives and press releases. Plan for a heavier, multi-source pipeline for the single most important association in the cell.

description: https://www.czech-ba.cz/cs returned HTTP 403 Forbidden to automated fetch, despite ČNB citing czech-ba.cz as ČBA's official URL and search results surfacing live-looking subpages (/en/about-cba, /cs/o-cba/komise-pracovni-organy).

result.result_summary: Bot defence hypothesis, not a dead site. Not recorded as dead.

why_it_matters: If czech-ba.cz holds archived ČBA documents that cbaonline.cz dropped, an automated crawler will silently miss them. Requires browser-based or Wayback-based collection.

description: https://www.cbaonline.cz/kodexy-a-standardy served a 'Page not found' page while https://cbaonline.cz/kodexy-a-standardy is indexed and live; conversely /o-nas/komise-pracovni-skupiny surfaced under the www host.

result.result_summary: www vs non-www routing on cbaonline.cz is inconsistent per path.

why_it_matters: A crawler normalising to one host form will generate false 404s and could wrongly mark ČBA sections dead. Canonicalisation must be tested per path, and a 404 on one host must trigger a retry on the other before any liveness verdict.

description: The ČLFA stanoviska page's visible items span 2015-2021, most recent being a joint memorandum on CCD dated 3 December 2021 — yet ČLFA was demonstrably active on the CCD2 consumer credit amendment in March 2026 via press releases.

result.result_summary: The formal positions library lags the association's actual advocacy by years; current positions are being issued as press releases instead.

why_it_matters: Monitoring only the stanoviska section would produce a false 'ČLFA inactive' signal. Press releases (/pro-media/tiskove-zpravy) must be the primary ČLFA channel, with stanoviska as the archive.

description: Czech FinTech Association (ČEFTAS): searches in both cs and en for consultation responses or position papers on PSD3/PSR returned no association-authored position document. Its own site navigation shows only Home / About / Projects / Members / Contact / Membership plus articles, a podcast and a newsletter.

result.result_summary: ČEFTAS advocacy appears to be conducted informally (direct dialogue with MF ČR/ČNB) rather than through published stanoviska.

why_it_matters: For fintech-side regulatory positions, expect to rely on podcast/newsletter/article content, member law firms (e.g. FINREG PARTNERS, ARROWS) and MF ČR consultation summaries rather than association documents.

description: SBK operates a private member portal at data.bankovnikarty.cz/secure/private.htm; ČLFA has a /pro-cleny area. Member circulars — explicitly part of this cell's brief — appear to live behind these gates.

result.result_summary: Member circulars are not publicly accessible for SBK or ČLFA; no attempt was made to access gated areas.

why_it_matters: The 'member circulars' element of the cell is structurally uncollectable from open sources. It must be substituted by press releases, seminar agendas and ODOK comment tables, or obtained through legitimate membership/subscription.

description: No Czech-language term was found for a formal 'consultation response' artefact type published by ČBA; the domestic vocabulary is 'připomínky' / 'vypořádání připomínek' (comments in the inter-ministerial procedure) rather than the EU-style 'stanovisko ke konzultaci'. 'Stanovisko' in CZ financial-market usage most often denotes a ČNB supervisory opinion, not an industry position.

result.result_summary: Term ambiguity: 'stanovisko' is a noisy query term that returns ČNB supervisory opinions rather than association positions.

why_it_matters: Query design for this cell must prefer 'připomínky', 'připomínkové řízení', 'vypořádání připomínek', 'memorandum', 'pozice' over 'stanovisko' when targeting associations, and reserve 'stanovisko' for ČLFA/AKAT where it is their own section label.

description: No association in this cell was found to publish a dedicated REGULATORY DEADLINE calendar (transposition dates, effective dates, consultation closing dates). ČBA and AKAT publish event calendars only; SBK publishes conference/seminar announcements.

result.result_summary: Event calendars exist (cbaonline.cz/o-nas/kalendar, akatcr.cz/Dokumenty/Kalendar-udalosti); regulatory deadline calendars do not.

why_it_matters: The 'regulatory event calendar' element of the cell brief must be constructed by inference from event titles plus ODOK/MF ČR milestones, not harvested ready-made.

description: No dedicated, recurring KPMG Czech Republic 'FS Regulatory Update' series was found, in either cs or en. KPMG Germany runs exactly such a subscription newsletter (kpmg.com/de .../abo-kpmg-fs-regulatory-update.html), which suggests the format exists in the network but was not located for CZ.

result.result_summary: Only a general KPMG CZ banking industry hub (kpmg.com/cz/cs/odvetvi/bankovnictvi.html) was identified; no dated regulatory-update series.

why_it_matters: KPMG is one of the four named Big Four targets for this cell; without a periodic series its CZ coverage must be collected opportunistically, and EY/Deloitte carry the periodic load.

description: For A&O Shearman, Clifford Chance, White & Case, Dentons and Bird & Bird Prague, no Czech-jurisdiction regulatory client-alert stream was located — only office/practice/people pages and transaction press releases.

result.result_summary: International firms in Prague appear to publish regulatory content at group level (EU/global), not as CZ-tagged alerts discoverable via search.

why_it_matters: The 'local trigger date stated plainly' value proposition of this cell comes mainly from domestic firms and Big Four CZ, not from the international offices; collection design should weight accordingly.

description: No RSS feed, Atom feed, or machine-readable subscription endpoint was confirmed for any source in this cell. Email newsletter subscription is referenced by Deloitte CZ and HAVEL & PARTNERS but the mechanics (form URL, archive availability) were not verified.

result.result_summary: Push-delivery channels are advertised but unverified; all collection designs above assume HTML crawling.

why_it_matters: Adviser alerts are time-critical; if RSS/email archives exist, they would cut latency and crawl cost substantially. Worth a dedicated feed-discovery pass.

description: The Deloitte CZ 'Regulatorní novinky' page redirected (302) from www2.deloitte.com to www.deloitte.com, and the redirect target returned 404 on a single fetch.

result.result_summary: Treated as a domain-migration artefact (content likely relocated under /cz-sk/), not as a dead source.

why_it_matters: Recording it dead would drop one of the two periodic Big Four CZ regulatory digests; the deterministic verification pass must resolve the correct canonical path.

description: No Czech adviser was found publishing a structured, machine-readable regulatory deadline tracker (table/calendar of obligation dates) as a standing free product; deadlines appear embedded in prose alerts, PDFs, and seminar agendas.

result.result_summary: Closest artefacts are the Lexology 'What's on the horizon for 2026?' format and Pierstone's DORA obligations PDF.

why_it_matters: Deadline extraction will have to be NLP-over-prose rather than structured ingestion; budget for that in the collection design.

description: Czech-language searching for Visa/Mastercard scheme mandates aimed at CZ acquirers ('mandát', 'pravidla schémat', 'compliance termín') returned no Czech-language scheme-issued rule source. The schemes publish rules only in English; the visa.cz page is a thin consumer-facing pointer.

result.result_summary: Only English scheme rulebooks (visa-rules-public.pdf, mastercard-rules.pdf) and CZ acquirer merchant manuals surfaced; no CZ-language card-scheme rulebook exists as far as the search showed.

why_it_matters: Card-scheme deadlines affecting CZ actors must be tracked in English at source and cross-read against CZ acquirer manuals; a Czech-only monitoring strategy would miss them entirely.

description: No public, CZ-specific compilation of card-scheme mandate calendars (Visa/Mastercard release deadlines as they apply to Czech acquirers/merchants) was found. Trade-press and consultancy blogs (decta, cardcorp, beastinsights) discuss 2026 VAMP and Mastercard scam-merchant rules generically, not for CZ.

result.result_summary: Only vendor/consultancy commentary, no CZ-scoped mandate calendar.

why_it_matters: This is a real coverage hole: the deadline calendar must be reconstructed from the global rulebook editions plus acquirer bulletins rather than read off a ready list.

description: The Bank iD developer portal (technical specification, sandbox, API changelog) is referenced repeatedly as the place where the binding technical documentation lives, but it appears to sit behind registration; no unauthenticated URL for the spec was confirmed during this pass.

result.result_summary: Public site describes the developer portal; the portal itself was not reached or verified in this pass.

why_it_matters: The dated technical obligations for Bank iD integrators may only be observable to registered partners, limiting automated collection to the public contractual annexes.

description: COBS version numbering is reported inconsistently across secondary sources (versions 3.0/3.1/4.1/5.0/6.0 documented, with 'version 8' mentioned in discussion). The authoritative current version was not confirmed from the ČBA page or the GitHub repo in this pass.

result.result_summary: Conflicting version claims in aggregator/secondary sources; primary confirmation deferred.

why_it_matters: Deadline tracking for COBS must be anchored on the GitHub releases/tags rather than on ČBA prose or third-party summaries.
